results.description:
Amb. Mairo Abbas hosts NACCIMA delegation to dinner in Guangzhou, restates support for stronger Nigeria-China relations

The Consul General of the Federal Republic of Nigeria in Guangzhou, Amb. Mairo Musa Abbas, has pledged her continued support for the mission of the Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture (@NACCIMA30 ) to facilitate Chinese investments in Nigeria for accelerated industrial development.

The Consul General stated that foreign direct investment is key to achieving the $1 trillion economy aspiration of His Excellency President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

Amb. Mairo Abbas made this known when she hosted NACCIMA delegation led by the National President, Engr. Jani Ibrahim, mni, OON, to a dinner following the successful NACCIMA B2B Investment Forum 3.0 in Guangzhou as well as the Hainan Free Trade Port International Conference 2026.

The delegation included top Chamber executives, investors, businessmen, and professionals.

Amb. Mairo Abbas played leading roles in ensuring the success of the NACCIMA events through series of engagements with various associations of Chinese investors such as the China Chamber for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT), China Chamber of International Commerce (CCOIC), amongst others.

The Consul General said the Consulate will continue to support efforts targeted at strengthening the relationship that exists between Nigeria and China, extending it beyond trade and emphasising more on investment, technology transfer, and knowledge exchange.

She commended the National President of NACCIMA, Engr. Jani Ibrahim, for his exemplary leadership, courage, and can-do spirit, which is putting Nigeria on the map for international investment collaborations.

In his own remarks, Engr. Ibrahim appreciated the Consul General for the warm reception she has accorded to the NACCIMA delegation upon arrival in Guangzhou, while also commending her for the unwavering support she has offered the association for its mission in China.

The dinner further underscored the effective and healthy working relationship between NACCIMA and the Consulate, as both parties work towards one common goal.

results.title: Nigeria gets both, but mostly loans.
results.description: Nigeria gets both, but mostly loans. China has financed major rail projects (Abuja-Kaduna, Lagos-Ibadan, Kaduna-Kano) with billions in loans from Exim Bank and CDB. Nigeria still owes China about $5.7 billion. Smaller grants also happen, like the recent $30 million RMB 200m for community projects. Overall pattern matches the rest of Africa: loans dominate, pure aid is limited.
